newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to tackle problem loans for recovery - Kubo.
newsitem.headline: Japan to tackle problem loans for recovery - Kubo.

text.p: Japan will try to strengthen its economic recovery and make it sustainable by steadily implementing this year's state budget and dealing quickly with problem loans at financial firms, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said in a speech on Friday.

Kubo's speech, read out by Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa at a national convention of credit unions, said Japan's economy was still recovering on the back of steady private-sector demand, although the pace remained gradual.
"There is a worrisome factor in that employment conditions, although improving, remain severe," Kubo said.
Credit unions, which cater to small firms and individuals, are expected to play an important role in serving the specific needs of a particular region, Kubo said.
Credit unions are small financial institutions which take deposits and lend money mainly to members.

"It is very regrettable that several credit unions have failed in the last two years from lax management which deviates from the ideology of credit unions, such as violating rules on large loans and on deals with non-members," he said.
The ministry has been adjusting the existing system for healthier management at credit unions by strengthening their supervisory and inspection mechanisms, Kubo said.
He urged credit unions to beef up their supervisory and risk mangement systems, boost their self-owned capital and tackle problem loans with vigour.
